text: Okay, so what actually happens when you type cookie into Google? Let's follow it.
So the second you type that first letter, your browser's like, wait, where's Google? And it asks DNS, which is basically the internet's phone book.
Then it sets up an encrypted connection, so nobody in between can see what you're typing.
And now every single letter you type? That's a tiny request. And the suggestions come right back.
You hit Enter, and your search flies off to Google. Oh, and your cookies? Yeah, they tag along too. [chuckle]
Now, inside a data center, thousands of machines search their own little piece of the index, all at the same time.
Then everything gets ranked. Relevance, quality, all that stuff. And the best results float to the top.
And then the results fly back, and your browser draws the page.
All of that, in a fraction of a second. Pretty wild, right?
